entities.name: Dorotea Bucca
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Dorotea Bucca (d. 1436) was a pioneering Italian physician and philosopher who flourished at the University of Bologna for over four decades, beginning in 1390.

Her association with the university has been subject to debate, with some arguing that she taught or held a position there, while others claim she merely studied medicine and philosophy. Despite these disputes, Dorotea's contributions to medical knowledge and her influence on feminist thought are undeniable.

As one of the first female physicians in Europe, Dorotea's work paved the way for future generations of women in medicine, challenging the patriarchal norms of her time.

In addition to her academic achievements, Dorotea was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the city of Bologna, leaving behind a lasting legacy that continues to inspire scholars today.

The exact dates of her birth are unknown, but it is clear that Dorotea Bucca lived a life marked by intellectual curiosity, courage, and determination.
